entries.desc: The document says documentation and decision-doc audit use the same ordinary REVIEW default as other development work.

evidence.note: The document purpose and Documentation Audit Unified Rule state that documentation and decision-doc audit use the same default REVIEW path as ordinary development. The assertion command printed: doc policy and English-only checks passed.

entries.desc: The document says documentation and decision-doc audit escalate to 3x2 only when the first REVIEW round records at least two countable problems.

evidence.note: The DONE Gate section now defines the target formula as requires3x2 = firstReviewRoundCountableProblems >= 2, and the test matrix says zero or one countable first-round finding does not require 3x2.

entries.desc: The document states current code may still enforce legacy decision-doc 3x2 until the implementation story updates the gate.

evidence.note: The purpose, current-state table, documentation audit rule, and DONE Gate transition note explicitly say current runtime may still enforce legacy direct decision-doc 3x2 until a follow-up implementation story migrates the gate.

entries.desc: The document says documentation audit can use the same explicit degraded 3x1 fallback when allowed by policy or approval.

evidence.note: The degraded fallback rule and decision-doc tests state that escalated documentation audit may use approved degraded 3x1 only with assuranceLevel=degraded-single-host and without claiming full 3x2.

entries.desc: The document no longer preserves always-on decision-doc 3x2 as the desired target policy.

evidence.note: The old purpose line Always-on: direct decision-doc changes still require 3 quorum rounds x 2 independent PASS hosts is absent. Decision-doc changes with zero countable first-round findings are now expected to require3x2=false under the target policy.

entries.desc: The document does not claim the automatic document-audit policy is already implemented in runtime code.

evidence.note: The document labels automatic document-audit behavior as the target policy and repeatedly says current implementation may still be legacy until the implementation story changes the runtime gate; it does not claim runtime implementation is already complete.
